The hero line can be Your night, your choice, your story. Other captions can include Curiosity is part of growing up, Make a memory you actually want to keep, New experience, clear boundaries, and Ask first, then decide for yourself. The images should show adults meeting friends, talking honestly, and choosing what feels right rather than portraying intoxication or sexual performance as a badge of popularity. In week one, creators can share a first-night story and invite followers to name something they are curious about. In week two, publish polls about trying an unfamiliar drink, meeting a new partner, or going to a party alone. Place a short reminder after each poll to check what is being offered, tell a trusted friend where you are, use protection where relevant, and stop if consent is absent or uncertain. In week three, launch a buddy check-in, ride-home planning, and a discreet page for testing, contraception, and emergency support. They should explain that intoxication and pressure invalidate consent, but they do not need to turn every caption into a lecture. Track resource visits, buddy-check-in completion, reports of pressure, and whether users feel more able to set boundaries, in addition to ordinary reach metrics. An adult-health reviewer should read the entire feed as a sequence, because a small safety footer can be overwhelmed by aspirational headlines. If the feed would reasonably be understood as urging people to take drugs or have sex, remove that post rather than relying on a disclaimer. The brand can celebrate candid adult conversation, but it should not imply that experimentation is required for belonging or that saying no is a failure.

Add jurisdiction-specific contacts, records-preservation guidance, and assurance against retaliation for good-faith reports.
